name: Odds in one arm
expression: odds_T = a / b ;  odds_C = c / d
variables: a = treatment-arm events; b = treatment-arm non-events; c = control-arm events; d = control-arm non-events; odds_T, odds_C = odds of the event in the treatment and control arm.
notes: Worked: Watson 1999, odds(LAF) = 5/49 = 0.10204, odds(LPF) = 5/48 = 0.10417. Odds are not probabilities (the book warns against using the terms interchangeably, p. 97).

name: Sample odds ratio
expression: OR_hat = theta_hat = (a/b) / (c/d) = (a·d) / (b·c)
variables: a, b = events and non-events in the treatment arm; c, d = events and non-events in the control arm; n1 = a + b; n2 = c + d; OR_hat = sample odds ratio (treatment arm in the numerator).
notes: [R] The printed fraction is scrambled in the DOCX conversion; reconstructed from the worked value (20/60)/(80/20) = 1/12 = 0.083333. effect_sizes.two_by_two('OR', e1, n1, e2, n2) returns ln OR and its variance (takes events and arm totals, not non-events), adds 0.5 to all cells only if a zero cell exists and by default drops double-zero studies; the chapter has no zero-cell handling.

name: Log odds ratio and back-transformation
expression: theta*_hat = ln(OR_hat) ;  OR = exp(theta*)
variables: OR_hat = sample odds ratio; theta*_hat = natural log of the OR (approximately normally distributed); exp = exponential back-transformation to the OR scale.
notes: All inference (CI, tests, pooling) is done on the ln scale; only CI limits and point estimates are back-transformed. The log transformation does not change the test statistic or P-value. Worked: ln(1/12) = −2.48490665.

name: Variance and standard error of ln OR (Woolf)
expression: Var(theta*_hat) = 1/a + 1/b + 1/c + 1/d ;  SE(theta*_hat) = sqrt(1/a + 1/b + 1/c + 1/d)
variables: a, b, c, d = 2×2 cell counts (treatment events, treatment non-events, control events, control non-events); theta*_hat = ln OR.
notes: [R] Printed fragments read '1 … 111 … a + b + c + d'; confirmed numerically: SE = 0.359397644 for (20, 60, 80, 20) and Var = 0.4412 for Watson 1999 (5, 49, 5, 48). Undefined with a zero cell; the chapter gives no continuity correction.

name: Wald confidence interval for an individual OR
expression: LL* = theta*_hat − z_{α/2}·SE(theta*_hat) ;  UL* = theta*_hat + z_{α/2}·SE(theta*_hat) ;  LL = exp(LL*) ;  UL = exp(UL*)
variables: theta*_hat = ln OR; SE = Woolf SE; z_{α/2} = standard normal critical value (1.96 for 95%); LL*, UL* = limits on the ln scale; LL, UL = limits on the OR scale.
notes: effect_sizes.study_ci returns the ln-scale limits; exponentiate (effect_sizes.back_transform) for the OR scale. Worked: (20, 60, 80, 20) gives 95% CI (0.0412, 0.1686). OR-scale limits are asymmetric around the OR.

name: Wald z-test for ln OR
expression: H0: theta* = ln OR = 0 (OR = 1) ;  Z = theta*_hat / SE(theta*_hat) ~ N(0,1) ;  P = 2·P(Z > |z0|) ;  reject H0 if |z0| ≥ z_{α/2} or P ≤ α
variables: theta*_hat = ln OR (single study or pooled); SE = its standard error; z0 = observed value of Z; α = significance level; z_{α/2} = critical value.
notes: Used for individual studies and for FE, RE and IVhet pooled estimates. Worked: (20, 60, 80, 20) gives z = −6.914, P ≈ 0. Typos in the source: 'H0: θ = 0' uses θ for the OR (p. 94) and 'P(|Z| > −2.18)' should read P(|Z| > 2.18) (p. 95). The book reads P from z tables (2 × 0.0146 = 0.0292).

name: Inverse-variance weight and percent weight
expression: w_i = 1 / v_i ;  %W_i = 100 · w_i / Σ_j w_j
variables: v_i = Var(ln OR_i), the within-study variance of study i; w_i = inverse-variance (FE) weight; %W_i = percent weight shown in the forest plot.
notes: models.meta_analysis returns weights_pct. MetaXL prints % weight to 1 decimal. IVhet uses the same weights as FE; RE uses w_i* = 1/(v_i + τ²).

name: Fixed-effect (inverse-variance) pooled ln OR (Eq. 5.1)
expression: theta*_FE = Σ_{i=1..k} w_i·theta*_i / Σ_{i=1..k} w_i
variables: theta*_i = ln OR of study i; w_i = 1/v_i; k = number of studies; theta*_FE = pooled ln OR under the common-effect model theta_hat_i = theta + ε_i, ε_i ~ N(0, σ_i²).
notes: Call models.meta_analysis(yi, vi, model='fixed', ci_method='z'). Worked (thyroid): Σw = 49.6944, Σw·ln OR = −15.364, theta*_FE = −0.3092, OR 0.73. MetaXL model code 'IV'.

name: Fixed-effect variance, SE, CI and test
expression: Var(theta*_FE) = 1/Σ w_i ;  SE = sqrt(1/Σ w_i) ;  CI = exp(theta*_FE ± z_{α/2}·SE) ;  Z = theta*_FE / SE
variables: w_i = inverse-variance weights; theta*_FE = pooled ln OR; z_{α/2} = 1.96 for 95%; Z = Wald test statistic for H0: ln OR = 0.
notes: Worked (thyroid): SE = 0.141856, z0 = −2.1794, P = 0.0292 from tables (exact 0.0293), OR 0.73 (0.56, 0.97). The formula line on p. 94 wrongly shows the SE as 0.148156; the reported z uses 0.141856.

name: Random-effects model specification
expression: theta_hat_i = theta + ς_i + ε_i ;  ς_i ~ N(0, τ²) ;  ε_i ~ N(0, σ_i²) ;  Var(theta_hat_i) = σ_i² + τ²
variables: theta = mean effect; ς_i = theta_i − theta, between-study deviation of study i; τ² = between-study variance; ε_i = within-study error with variance σ_i² (estimated by v_i).
notes: The book estimates τ² only with the DerSimonian–Laird method of moments. Engine default for model='random' is REML with an HKSJ CI; pass tau2_method='DL', ci_method='z' to reproduce the book.

name: Random-effects total variance and weight
expression: v_i* = v_i + τ²_hat ;  w_i* = 1 / (v_i + τ²_hat)
variables: v_i = within-study variance of ln OR_i; τ²_hat = estimated between-study variance (DL); v_i* = total variance; w_i* = random-effects weight.
notes: Worked (heartburn): τ² = 0.1852 gives Σw* = 10.8299 in Table 5.7 (exact 10.8304 with τ² = 0.185173). [note: the book claims smaller studies get higher weights under RE; in fact w_i* stays monotone in v_i and the weights only become more equal (heartburn: Hagedorn 28.6% → 23.3%, Raue 2.9% → 4.1%, ranking unchanged).]

name: Random-effects pooled ln OR (Eq. 5.2), SE and CI
expression: theta*_RE = Σ w_i*·theta*_i / Σ w_i* ;  SE(theta*_RE) = sqrt(1/Σ w_i*) ;  CI = exp(theta*_RE ± z_{α/2}·SE) ;  Z = theta*_RE / SE
variables: w_i* = 1/(v_i + τ²_hat); theta*_i = ln OR of study i; z_{α/2} = 1.96 for 95%.
notes: Use models.meta_analysis(yi, vi, model='random', tau2_method='DL', ci_method='z'). Worked (heartburn): theta*_RE = 0.6614, SE = 0.30387, z = 2.17659, OR 1.94 (1.07, 3.51). The book's CI uses the rounded 0.66 and prints '0.54' (typo) in UL* (p. 102); exact CI (1.0680, 3.5146). MetaXL model code 'RE'.

name: Cochran's Q (computational form)
expression: Q = Σ w_i·theta*_i² − (Σ w_i·theta*_i)² / Σ w_i  [= Σ w_i·(theta*_i − theta*_FE)²]
variables: theta*_i = ln OR of study i; w_i = 1/v_i (FE weights); theta*_FE = FE pooled ln OR; H0: theta_1 = … = theta_k.
notes: Model-independent: identical in FE, RE and IVhet output. Worked: thyroid Q = 8.734434 − (−15.3636)²/49.69437 = 3.984578; heartburn Q = 16.4568 − 11.46928²/16.53557 = 8.50158.

name: P-value of Cochran's Q
expression: Q ~ χ²_{df} under H0 ;  df = k − 1 ;  P = P(χ²_{df} > Q)
variables: Q = Cochran's Q; k = number of studies; df = degrees of freedom.
notes: χ² tables only bracket the P-value (0.50–0.75 for the thyroid data); software gives the exact value (0.68). Heartburn: P = 0.20.

name: DerSimonian–Laird scaling constant C
expression: C = Σ w_i − Σ w_i² / Σ w_i
variables: w_i = 1/v_i, FE inverse-variance weights.
notes: models.heterogeneity returns it as 'C' (also computed inside models.tau2_dl). Worked (heartburn): 16.53557 − 50.03969/16.53557 = 13.50939.

name: DerSimonian–Laird estimator of τ²
expression: τ²_hat = (Q − df) / C ;  df = k − 1  (standard practice: τ²_hat = max(0, (Q − df)/C))
variables: Q = Cochran's Q with FE weights; df = k − 1; C = Σ w_i − Σ w_i²/Σ w_i; τ²_hat = between-study variance estimate.
notes: The chapter does not state truncation at 0; models.tau2_dl truncates. Thyroid: Q < df, so τ² = 0 and RE = FE. Heartburn: (8.502 − 6)/13.51 = 0.1852 (unrounded 0.185173). [note: Cochrane Handbook v6 prefers REML or Paule–Mandel (models.tau2_reml, models.tau2_pm).]

name: I² statistic
expression: I² = (Q − df) / Q × 100%, negative values truncated to 0%  [= max(0, (Q − df)/Q) × 100%]
variables: Q = Cochran's Q; df = k − 1.
notes: Interpreted as the percentage of variation across studies due to systematic heterogeneity rather than chance. Book typo: (3.98 − 6)/3.98 × 100% printed as '−0.51%' instead of −50.75%; final 0% correct after truncation. Heartburn: I² = 29%. No numeric thresholds in this chapter.

name: IVhet pooled ln OR
expression: theta*_IVhet = Σ w_i·theta*_i / Σ w_i ,  w_i = 1/v_i  (identical to theta*_FE)
variables: theta*_i = ln OR of study i; v_i = within-study variance; w_i = FE inverse-variance weight.
notes: Doi et al. (2015a). Called via models.meta_analysis(yi, vi, model='ivhet'). Point estimate and weights equal FE regardless of heterogeneity; heartburn ln OR = 11.46928/16.5356 = 0.693611, OR = 2.00. MetaXL model code 'IVhet'.

name: IVhet variance of the pooled ln OR
expression: Var(theta*_IVhet) = Σ_i (w_i / Σ_j w_j)² · (v_i + τ²_hat)
variables: w_i = 1/v_i (FE weights); v_i = within-study variance; τ²_hat = DerSimonian–Laird between-study variance from the FE-weighted Q.
notes: [R] Printed form heavily garbled; verified numerically: heartburn Var = 0.094364 (SE 0.307187) with τ² = 0.185173. Table 5.8's last column is headed 'W*(IVhet)' but contains the summands (w_i/Σw)²·V*_i, not weights. SE_IVhet ≥ SE_FE whenever τ² > 0.

name: IVhet confidence interval and test
expression: SE = sqrt(Var(theta*_IVhet)) ;  LL* = theta*_IVhet − z_{α/2}·SE ;  UL* = theta*_IVhet + z_{α/2}·SE ;  CI_OR = (exp(LL*), exp(UL*)) ;  Z = theta*_IVhet / SE
variables: theta*_IVhet = IVhet pooled ln OR; Var = IVhet variance; z_{α/2} = 1.96 for 95%.
notes: Worked (heartburn): the book centres the CI on 0.6931 rather than its own estimate 0.693611, giving LL* = 0.6931 − 1.96×0.307187 = 0.09101, UL* = 1.29519 and CI (1.09528, 3.65168); exact (1.0958, 3.6535); both round to (1.10, 3.65). Recomputed z = 2.258, P = 0.024 (not reported in the book). z-based; no t or HKSJ variant in the book.

name: Confidence-interval width on the OR scale
expression: width = UL − LL  (OR scale)
variables: UL, LL = upper and lower 95% CI limits of the pooled OR.
notes: Used to compare models on the heartburn data: FE 3.24 − 1.24 = 2.00, RE 3.51 − 1.07 = 2.44, IVhet 3.65 − 1.10 = 2.55. Because OR-scale CIs are asymmetric, width on the ln scale (2·z·SE) is a cleaner comparison.

name: Percentage reduction in odds
expression: reduction (%) = (1 − OR) × 100
variables: OR = odds ratio below 1 (numerator arm vs reference arm).
notes: Thyroid OR 0.73 means 27% lower odds in the high-dose (numerator) arm; the book's wording '0.27 times less odds' is incorrect phrasing for this quantity.

name: Subgroup weight share in MetaXL subgroup output
expression: %W_g = Σ_{i ∈ g} %W_i*(overall RE)
variables: g = subgroup; %W_i* = per-study percent weight from the overall random-effects analysis; %W_g = weight shown on the subgroup summary row.
notes: Extractor's verification, not stated in the book: Old studies 14.7 + 23.3 + 11.3 + 15.1 = 64.4%, Recent 12.5 + 4.1 + 19.0 = 35.6%. The subgroup pooled estimates themselves use a separate DL τ² per subgroup (0.3520 Old, 0 Recent). moderators.subgroup_analysis computes subgroup estimates and Q-between (0.97, df 1, P = 0.32 with separate DL τ²) but does not output this weight share.

name: Doi plot Z-score (reconstruction)
expression: sort studies by theta*_i ;  p_i = (Σ_{j<i} w_j + w_i/2) / Σ_j w_j ;  Z_i = Φ^{-1}(p_i) ;  plot |Z_i| (y) against theta*_i (x)
variables: theta*_i = ln OR of study i; w_i = 1/v_i (inverse-variance weights); p_i = weighted mid-rank percentile of study i; Φ^{-1} = standard normal quantile function; |Z_i| = Doi-plot ordinate.
notes: [R] Extractor's reconstruction; the chapter gives no formula. Reproduces the plotted heartburn |Z| = 2.18, 1.13, 0.53, 0.15, 0.16, 0.71, 1.67 (Raue, Cao, Watson 1999, Spence, Khan, Hagedorn, Watson 2004). The LFK index formula is not given in this chapter (printed value 1.61, minor asymmetry). The engine's bias.doi_plot_data implements the published metasens::lfkindex variant (N_j = 100·max(v)/v_j, percentile (MR_j − 0.5)/ΣN), which gives |Z| 2.19 and 1.66 for the two end studies and LFK 1.609; engine_ref stays null because that percentile definition differs from this reconstruction.
